patterns.name: Hardcoded secret or credential in Java source
patterns.description: A string literal that looks like a credential (JWT secret, API key, password, database URL) is assigned directly in source rather than loaded from environment variables, properties files, or a vault. This exposes credentials in version control and compiled artifacts.
patterns.message: Variable '{target}' in {file} contains what appears to be a hardcoded credential. Load secrets from System.getenv(), Spring @Value, or a vault instead.

patterns.name: Hardcoded fallback when environment variable is missing in Java
patterns.description: System.getenv() is called with a ternary or Optional fallback that provides a hardcoded credential when the environment variable is absent. This is a common configuration pattern that embeds credentials in source code.
patterns.message: '{target}' in {file} falls back to a hardcoded value when the environment variable is absent. Remove the fallback — throw an exception at startup if the required secret is not configured.
